title: 내가 직접 가봐야겠다  (I'll Have to Go Down Myself)

segments.t: Fed up with backstage interruptions, Cindy needles her road manager and refuses to change out of a sheer black stage outfit, forcing Tak Ye-jin to march down to the dressing rooms herself. Listen for the Korean words for 'picky' and 'stage outfit'.
다음 주 리허설 꼭 빼달라 그래.
근데 여기 메인 피디 엄청 까다로워서.
오빠가 보기에 난 안 까다로워?
미안하다.
뭐가 미안한데? 나 진짜 궁금해서 그래.
피디님, 저희 그냥 입어야 될 것 같습니다.
이거 안 되겠네, 내가 직접 가봐야겠다.
내가 어떻게 걔랑 싸우니? 혼내는 거지.
Let's unpack the eight lines of backstage tension before Cindy and Ye-jin collide.
다음 주 리허설 꼭 빼달라 그래.

'Tell them to definitely take me out of next week's rehearsal.' Slipping the word for 'without fail' before the request orders her manager to get her excused, using a word that means 'to pull out' or 'skip' Swap in this word.
근데 여기 메인 피디 엄청 까다로워서.
'The main PD here is super picky, though.' An everyday intensifier meaning 'hugely' or 'super' is paired with an word meaning 'fussy', 'demanding', or 'hard to please' We built from this.
오빠가 보기에 난 안 까다로워?

'In your eyes, am I not picky?' Even though Cindy is his boss, her manager is a few years older, so she addresses him with a woman's word for an older brother or older male colleague, followed by an expression meaning 'in someone's view' It is a handy word.
미안하다.

'I'm sorry.' Cornered, the manager blurts out a plain, casual 'sorry'. Unlike the formal apology, this casual form is used with younger people or close friends, though here it only digs his hole deeper! The word doubles the.
뭐가 미안한데? 나 진짜 궁금해서 그래.
'What are you sorry for? I'm asking because I'm genuinely curious.' Cindy pounces by asking what part he is sorry about, then follows up with a word meaning 'to be curious' This means that.
피디님, 저희 그냥 입어야 될 것 같습니다.

'PD, it looks like we'll just have to wear this.' Caught between two terrifying women, the manager bows to Ye-jin using the humble word for 'we' and the word 'to wear' in a polite pattern meaning 'it seems we must wear it' It is a handy word.
이거 안 되겠네, 내가 직접 가봐야겠다.

'This won't do, I'll have to go see her myself.' Ye-jin starts with a crisp Korean sigh meaning 'this isn't going to cut it', then pairs an word meaning 'in person' or 'firsthand' with a phrase meaning 'I had better go check' It is a handy word.
내가 어떻게 걔랑 싸우니? 혼내는 거지.

'How could I fight with her? I'm going to scold her.' When Il-yong asks if she plans to 'fight', Ye-jin laughs it off: adults don't fight kids, they scold them! Notice the word for. Now let's hear the whole backstage buildup again.
다음 주 리허설 꼭 빼달라 그래.
근데 여기 메인 피디 엄청 까다로워서.
오빠가 보기에 난 안 까다로워?
미안하다.
뭐가 미안한데? 나 진짜 궁금해서 그래.
피디님, 저희 그냥 입어야 될 것 같습니다.
이거 안 되겠네, 내가 직접 가봐야겠다.
내가 어떻게 걔랑 싸우니? 혼내는 거지.
You picked up the Korean words for picky, curious, in person, and scolding. Brace yourself for the dressing-room face-off!
안녕히 가세요!
